name: Thomas Merton Family Center
description: One of Bridgeport's anchor food sites, about a mile from campus: a free hot breakfast and lunch dining room on weekdays, plus the Connie's Eat Smart food pantry where registered guests shop for about five days of groceries once a month in a grocery-store-style setting. Also offers case management, showers, and a mail-address program.
nextStep: For meals, just walk in Mon-Fri. For the pantry, register on a Monday (10 a.m.-1 p.m.); shopping days are split by last name (Tue A-G, Wed H-P, Thu Q-Z).

name: SNAP Benefits — Free Application Help
description: SNAP puts a monthly food budget on an EBT card. Many students qualify under student exemptions (working 20+ hours a week, a work-study job, caring for a young child) and never apply. End Hunger Connecticut's SNAP Call Center gives free, confidential pre-screening and application help by phone, seven days a week.
nextStep: Call the SNAP Call Center at 866-974-SNAP (7627) for a free pre-screen, or apply online through CT DSS ConneCT.

nextStep: Open the city list to see every Bridgeport pantry with current hours.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Free, confidential, 24/7 support for anyone in emotional distress or suicidal crisis — call or text. Spanish-language support is available (988, then press 2); hearing impaired callers dial 711 then 988. Veterans press 1 for the Veterans Crisis Line or text 838255.
nextStep: Call or text 988 right now — a person answers 24/7.

name: Crisis Text Line
description: Free, confidential, 24/7 crisis support by text with a trained counselor — for students who would rather text than talk.
nextStep: Text HOME to 741741.

name: ACTION Line — Connecticut Mobile Crisis
description: Connecticut's 24/7 adult mobile crisis line, run through 2-1-1 (United Way of CT, which is also CT's 988 provider). Clinicians answer, and mobile crisis teams can come to where the person is. Also the fastest route into local mental health and substance use services.
nextStep: Call 2-1-1 and follow the crisis prompts, or call 1-800-467-3135 directly.

access.value: Phone, 24/7; mobile teams can respond in person

evidence.value: Phone, 24/7; mobile teams can respond in person

name: UB Clinics (Teaching Clinics)
description: UB's teaching clinics at the Health Sciences Center — chiropractic, naturopathic medicine, acupuncture, and dental hygiene — where health-science students treat patients under supervision. Open to the public at reduced teaching-clinic fees; a realistic option for students without coverage.
nextStep: Call the UB Clinics reception to ask about current fees and appointments for the clinic you need.

name: Southwest Community Health Center — Behavioral Health
description: Federally qualified health center offering behavioral health care alongside primary care on a sliding fee scale. Its clinicians also staff services at the Thomas Merton Family Center part of the week — an off-campus option for ongoing care outside the university.
nextStep: Call 203-330-6000 and ask for behavioral health intake at the Bridgeport site nearest you.

name: Southwest Connecticut Mental Health System
description: The state-operated (CT DMHAS) local mental health authority for the greater Bridgeport area: outpatient mental health and co-occurring mental health + substance use treatment, including young-adult programs. This is the public-system destination for ongoing care.
nextStep: Reach this system through 2-1-1 / the ACTION Line, which routes Bridgeport residents here.

cost.note: Medicaid, Medicare, state and private insurance; payment assistance listed in federal facility data

name: St. Vincent's Behavioral Health — Bridgeport
description: Hospital-based inpatient and outpatient behavioral health and addiction treatment — a step up in intensity from campus counseling when a student needs structured care.
nextStep: Call 203-362-3900 (a live person answers) or 475-210-4416 for appointments and inquiries.

name: The Center for Family Justice
description: Free, confidential services for victims of domestic violence and sexual assault — crisis help, counseling, advocacy, and legal support — serving Bridgeport, Easton, Fairfield, Monroe, Stratford, and Trumbull.
nextStep: Call 203-334-6154 during office hours (Mon-Fri 9-5), or the 24/7 domestic violence hotline 1-800-799-7233 any time.

name: The Child & Family Guidance Center
description: Culturally responsive mental health services for children, teens, and families, regardless of ability to pay. Most relevant for UB students who are also parents, or who are supporting younger siblings.
nextStep: Call 203-394-6529 to ask about intake for your child or family.

name: Substance Use Treatment — Bridgeport
description: Local addiction treatment for students whose alcohol or drug use has become a problem: outpatient and intensive outpatient programs, medication-assisted treatment, and residential options. Liberation Programs' Bridgeport site is at 399 Mill Hill Avenue; Recovery Network of Programs runs the Kinsella Treatment Center at 1862 Commerce Drive. UB Counseling also supports students with alcohol and drug concerns and can make the referral — often the least intimidating first step.
nextStep: Start with UB Counseling (203-576-4454) for a referral, or call the ACTION Line via 2-1-1 for same-day direction.

cost.note: Both providers accept Medicaid per federal facility data; ask about assistance
